seo.title: A home temple, 3D-printed in pieces
seo.description: Navin's proudest personal project: a home temple (mandir) designed in Onshape, split into printable pieces with alignment pins and tab-and-slot joints, and printed through tens of failed runs.

title: A home temple, 3D-printed in pieces
summary: My proudest personal project: a mandir (home temple) designed in Onshape and printed piece by piece. It holds my murti.

hero.alt: The finished white 3D-printed temple with lattice panels and an Om pattern, with murtis inside

chapters.title: I taught myself CAD for it
body: A class conflicted with the CAD course, so I taught myself Onshape and asked a Truman professor for access to the 3D printer room and software. My first print was a cube with my name and the Truman logo.

chapters.title: The printer was too small
body: So I split the design with cut planes into pieces, joined with colored alignment pins and tab-and-slot joints. The idea came from a flat-pack wooden mandir I'd seen sold online.
The design has jali lattice panels, an Om in a radial pattern, a tiled hip roof and a tiered finial.

image.alt: Front of the temple showing the jali lattice and a radial Om pattern on the back wall

chapters.title: Tens of failed prints
body: It took months, including weeks of printing and tens of failed runs: a small, unreliable printer, filament jams, power cuts. The pieces still needed sanding and trimming to fit.
Only later, in WashU's CAD course, did I learn the tolerances that would have made them fit the first time.

image.alt: Side view of the temple showing the lattice side panel, the hip roof and the finial

quote: Experience makes problems go away, but struggling makes sure you know how and why.
